title: Wi-Fi Photo Frames: A Holiday Gift Grandparents Will Use Every Day
subtitle: How family-shared digital frames work, what they cost after the box is opened, and how to set one up before you wrap it.
excerpt: A Wi-Fi photo frame lets the whole family send new pictures straight to Grandma's living room. Here is how Aura, Skylight and Nixplay compare on price, fees and setup.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: The grandkids grow an inch every time you blink, and most of their pictures live on someone else's phone. A Wi-Fi photo frame fixes that. Family members send pictures from their phones, and new photos simply show up on a frame in the grandparents' living room, with no cables, memory cards or computer required.

That makes these frames one of the more thoughtful holiday gifts for grandparents. But the frames differ in ways that matter: some have touchscreens, some charge a yearly fee for extras, and all of them need a little setup. Here is what to know before you wrap one.

Each frame connects to the home's Wi-Fi and pulls in photos from the maker's online service. Family members add pictures through a free phone app, and some frames also accept photos by email. Aura says its frames can even receive photos sent by text message. The person who owns the frame does not need to touch a phone at all, which is the whole point.

If the grandparents don't have home internet, these frames won't receive new pictures. Skylight says its frame keeps showing the photos it already has without Wi-Fi, but it needs a connection to get new ones. Aura's specifications call for a 2.4GHz router, which most home routers offer, so it is worth confirming before you buy.

This is where the brands differ most. Aura says there are no subscriptions or fees for its frames and that you can add unlimited photos and videos. Skylight's basic photo sharing is free; its optional Plus plan costs $39 a year and adds features such as photo albums, changing frame settings from the app, and mirroring a slideshow to a TV. Nixplay's free plan includes 500 MB of photo storage and one shared album. Its paid plans run $19.99 a year for 100 GB, or $29.99 a year for Nixplay Plus with unlimited photo storage. Nixplay states that the subscription is optional.
Before you gift it: a setup checklist

items: Ask about Wi-Fi first, and get the network name and password if you will be doing the setup in person.
Preload photos before the box is opened. Aura, Skylight and Nixplay all describe ways to load pictures before the frame is first plugged in, so it shows family photos right away.
Invite the family. Add children and grandchildren to the frame's app or share its email address so new photos keep coming after the holidays.
Decide who is the frame's helper. Choose one family member to handle settings, sleep times and any fee-based plan.
Pick a spot near an outlet. These frames plug into the wall, so a side table or kitchen counter near a socket works best.
Think about touch. A touchscreen lets the grandparent swipe back to a favorite picture; a frame without one is simpler but less hands-on.

sections.content: All three below have screens of about 10 inches and work through a free phone app. Prices are what each maker listed in October 2026 and may change during holiday sales. We have not tested these frames ourselves; the details come from the makers' own pages.

Aura's Carver is the choice if you want no fees at all and the simplest experience for the grandparent. Its controls are a touch bar on the frame rather than a full touchscreen, and the Aura app is required for setup. Skylight's frame has a 10-inch touchscreen for pinching, cropping and zooming, and it lets family send photos by email without an account or subscription, which helps relatives who would rather not install another app. Nixplay's Classic frame also has a touchscreen and accepts photos from its app, the web or a dedicated email address, but its free storage is limited, so a busy family may end up paying for a plan.

sections.label: Good to Know
sections.content: Photos sent to these frames are stored on the maker's online service, not just on the frame. Before you invite the whole family, talk about which pictures belong on Grandma's coffee table. Look through the app's settings with the frame's helper so you know who can add photos and how to remove one.

The best digital frame is the one the family will actually keep filling. Settle the Wi-Fi question, preload a few dozen favorite photos, and get everyone on the app before the holidays. Then the gift keeps arriving all year, one picture at a time.

products.name: Carver 10"
products.blurb: A 10.1-inch frame (1280 x 800) with no subscription fees and unlimited photo and video storage, according to Aura. Family can add photos from the app, email or by text, and you can preload photos before it is delivered.

products.name: The Skylight Frame (10-inch)
products.blurb: A 10-inch color touchscreen frame. Family can send photos through the free app or by email with no account or subscription required; the optional Plus plan is $39 a year.

products.name: Classic 10.1" HD Touch Screen
products.blurb: A matted 10.1-inch touchscreen frame that takes photos from the Nixplay app, the web or a dedicated email address. The free plan includes 500 MB of photo storage; paid plans are optional.
